the stage of correcting and improving software after release
a rough working version made to test understanding early
the stage of deciding the structure, data and interfaces of the system
items.s: Prototype: a rough working version made to test understanding early. The other options describe Maintenance, Design, Sprint.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Implementation.
o: a fixed short period in which an agreed set of work is completed
the stage of writing and assembling the code
the stage of putting the software into real use
the stage of discovering what the software must do
items.s: Implementation: the stage of writing and assembling the code. The other options describe Requirement gathering, Deployment, Sprint.

items.q: In this course, Constant refers to
o: a named value that does not change while a program runs
explanatory text in code that the machine ignores
a finite ordered set of steps that solves a problem
a named storage place whose value may change while a program runs
items.s: Constant: a named value that does not change while a program runs. The other options describe Variable, Comment, Algorithm.

items.q: “a separate line of development that can be merged later” is the definition of
o: Stand up meeting
Backup
Commit
Branch
items.s: Branch is a separate line of development that can be merged later.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Compiler.
o: the human written form of a program
a language close to machine instructions, such as assembly
a language written in human readable terms that needs translation
a program that translates source code into machine code before running
items.s: Compiler: a program that translates source code into machine code before running. The other options describe Low level language, Source code, High level language.

items.q: “the rules that govern how a program's statements must be written” is the definition of
o: Source code
Syntax
Compiler
Integrated development environment
items.s: Syntax is the rules that govern how a program's statements must be written.

items.q: “the person who actually works with the finished software” is the definition of
o: Technical debt
End user
Maintainability
Stakeholder
items.s: End user is the person who actually works with the finished software.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Software product.
o: the ease with which software can be understood and changed later
a service or constraint the software must satisfy
the person or organisation for whom software is built
software built for others to use, with its documentation and support
items.s: Software product: software built for others to use, with its documentation and support. The other options describe Requirement, Maintainability, Client.

items.q: The correct meaning of Condition is
o: choosing between paths according to a condition
the kind of value a variable holds, such as number or text
an expression that evaluates to true or false
repeating a block of instructions while a condition holds
items.s: Condition: an expression that evaluates to true or false. The other options describe Selection, Data type, Iteration.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Testing.
o: a fixed short period in which an agreed set of work is completed
the stage of checking that the software behaves as intended
the stage of studying requirements for consistency and feasibility
an approach of short repeated cycles delivering working software often
items.s: Testing: the stage of checking that the software behaves as intended. The other options describe Analysis, Agile development, Sprint.

items.q: Three of these relate to Teamwork and version control. Which one does not?
o: Repository
Variable
Commit
Version control
items.s: Every other option belongs to Teamwork and version control. “Variable” belongs to Programming logic, not Teamwork and version control.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Acceptance test.
o: a test by the client to decide whether the software may be accepted
the work of locating and correcting a defect
the controlled running of software to find defects
testing behaviour without knowledge of the internal code
items.s: Acceptance test: a test by the client to decide whether the software may be accepted. The other options describe Testing, Debugging, Black box testing.

items.q: “a program that translates source code into machine code before running” is the definition of
o: Syntax
Source code
Compiler
High level language
items.s: Compiler is a program that translates source code into machine code before running.

items.q: The correct meaning of Feasibility study is
o: the written record of what the system is agreed to do
a description of a sequence of actions between a user and the system
the unplanned growth of a project's requirements
the examination of whether a proposed system can be built in practice
items.s: Feasibility study: the examination of whether a proposed system can be built in practice. The other options describe Scope creep, Requirements specification, Use case.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a test of the whole system against its requirements”
o: System test
Integration test
Acceptance test
Edge case
items.s: System test is a test of the whole system against its requirements.

items.q: In this course, Requirement gathering refers to
o: the stage of discovering what the software must do
the stage of putting the software into real use
a significant point in the schedule marking completed work
the stage of checking that the software behaves as intended
items.s: Requirement gathering: the stage of discovering what the software must do. The other options describe Testing, Milestone, Deployment.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Ambiguity.
o: wording that can be read in more than one way
a statement of how well the system must behave, such as speed or safety
the written record of what the system is agreed to do
the quality of a requirement that can be checked by test
items.s: Ambiguity: wording that can be read in more than one way. The other options describe Requirements specification, Non functional requirement, Verifiability.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a statement of what the system must do”
o: Feasibility study
Functional requirement
Scope creep
User story
items.s: Functional requirement is a statement of what the system must do.

items.q: Use case may be defined as
o: a statement of how well the system must behave, such as speed or safety
a description of a sequence of actions between a user and the system
the examination of whether a proposed system can be built in practice
the written record of what the system is agreed to do
items.s: Use case: a description of a sequence of actions between a user and the system. The other options describe Feasibility study, Non functional requirement, Requirements specification.
